//racing: The key of a live round this person is sitting in, so the other can
join the same one. See the note on Presence in src/data/types.ts —
an asynchronous round names itself from the date, a live one cannot,
so the invitation goes down the channel that is already live.
//looking: The id of the memory this person has open in the Glasshouse. Same
channel and same reason as racing: there is no way to derive that
you are both in front of the same photograph, so it has to be said.
When the two match, the pane takes a warm edge and a cool one.
//driving: Her car on the road, while a live race is running: four integers in
the same encoding a recorded run is stored in, plus her own elapsed
race time on the end so the far side can work out her speed without
the network getting a vote in it. Sixteen writes a second while a car
is moving, and none of them matter a moment later, which is exactly
what this channel is for. See src/world/games/ember-rally/wire.ts.
